numerical_failure.observed_behavior: Nested trust-constr minimization crashes with ValueError: shapes (2,) and (4,) not aligned: 2 (dim 0) != 4 (dim 0) raised from _hessian_update_strategy.py update, because the default BFGS HessianUpdateStrategy object is shared between constraints and two nested minimizers update the same object.
numerical_failure.expected_behavior: Each NonlinearConstraint should get its own new BFGS object so nested minimizers do not share and corrupt one HessianUpdateStrategy; the minimization should complete without the shape error.
trigger_conditions: Nested optimize.minimize calls with method='trust-constr' where the outer objective calls an inner minimize that uses NonlinearConstraint with the default hess=BFGS()
Default BFGS object shared between constraints (mutable default argument in NonlinearConstraint.__init__)
Inner and outer problems have different dimensions (e.g. 2 and 4 variables) so the shared Hessian update produces mismatched shapes

input_output_examples.input: Nested example: outer optimize.minimize(beta, [4.0, 4.0, 2.0, 3.0], method='trust-constr', constraints=NonlinearConstraint(cd_contraint, 0, 0)); inner minimize over u0=[0.1, 0.1] with NonlinearConstraint(lsf, 0, 0) and hess=of_hess
input_output_examples.expected_output: Minimization completes and returns a result object (res.fun is produced) without a ValueError

oracle_clues: Traceback ends with ValueError raised at wMw = Mw.dot(w) in _hessian_update_strategy.py
PR test added in scipy/optimize/_trustregion_constr/tests/test_nested_minimize.py, verified to fail without commit 9b8c707
Fix changes default hess from BFGS() to None and constructs BFGS() inside __init__

category_specific_evidence: The passages describe a shared mutable default: the default BFGS() HessianUpdateStrategy in NonlinearConstraint.__init__ is one object shared across constraints, so two nested minimizers can both update the same object.
The PR fix changes the default to hess=None and constructs a new BFGS() inside __init__ when hess is None.
test_gh21193 asserts that constraint1.hess is not constraint2.hess, which checks that the default HUS objects are distinct.
The PR discussion says the new test fails without commit 9b8c707, which is the evidence that the test reproduces the sharing problem.
The passages give no numerical expected value, error magnitude, dtype, precision or tolerance for the violated property; the issue reproducer only prints the optimizer result res.
reproduction_risks: The reproducer in issue#21193 prints the scipy result object and gives no expected numerical values to compare against.
The test filters a warning about delta_grad == 0.0 and uses maxiter=2 for the inner minimizer, so the outcome depends on those settings.
The passages do not state a formula or invariant for the nested optimization that is violated numerically.
